action_items: Jordan: provide vector DB schema and 2 sample query workloads (due 2026-04-02)
summary: Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking architecture. Catalyst wants to evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for a hybrid dense+BM25 reranking pipeline. Key concerns: throughput (200 QPS target), index compatibility with their existing Postgres + FAISS flow, dimensionality tradeoffs, encryption/KMS, and SSO/SOC2 requirements.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. Diego from our infra/SE team will do the deep tech parts. Could you do quick intros?
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Yeah hey, Jordan, VP of Search at Catalyst. We own search and recommendations.
[00:14] Priya Shah: Priya, ML engineer, I work on embeddings and reranking models.
[00:18] Evan Moore: Evan, platform eng, I handle infra and DB side.
[00:22] Diego Ramos: Diego here, systems SE, hi.
[00:25] Maya Patel: Great. Objective: understand current infra, success criteria, timeline and capture blockers for hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:34] Jordan Lee: High level: we have a product search serving ~1.2M users. We want to move from a hybrid TF-IDF + LightGBM reranker to dense embeddings first-pass + lightweight reranker for final scoring. Need embeddings store + ANN index + rerank step.
[00:48] Priya Shah: Current setup: embeddings 1536-d from a base model, stored in Postgres for metadata and periodically exported to FAISS indexes. We run nightly rebuilds; QPS peaks at ~200 for search with bursts. Latency SLO < 120ms p95 for search end-to-end.
[01:10] Evan Moore: We also have a compliance requirement - SOC2 and SSO via Okta, KMS for key management, and data residency in eu-west-1 for EU customers.
[01:22] Maya Patel: Ok. Couple of clarifying Qs: is the 200 QPS sustained or burst? Also what's your target recall/latency tradeoff for reranking?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: Mostly sustained during daytime; bursts up to 400 for campaigns. For recall our product team wants top-10 for reranker candidates with high recall. End-to-end latency target is 120ms p95, but we can push to 200ms for heavy pages.
[01:45] Diego Ramos: On the Redwood side there are three deployment patterns to consider: Hosted API for quick integration, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for strict compliance. For 200 QPS with tight p95, Dedicated is often a sweet spot because it reduces noisy neighbor risk.
[02:05] Priya Shah: Important for us is the vector DB layer. We want to keep Postgres metadata but switch to FAISS or an external ANN - hoping to avoid migrating everything at once. How does Redwood integrate with vector DBs like FAISS or Pinecone?
[02:20] Diego Ramos: We support multiple patterns: Redwood can host embeddings and serve nearest-neighbor search directly (we have an ANN layer, HNSW/IVF+PQ options), or you can keep your vector DB and call Redwood for embeddings/rerank only. For FAISS specifically, many customers run a FAISS index and use Redwood for embeddings generation + rerank scoring; we also provide export/import helpers and a pluggable connector.
[02:45] Evan Moore: If we keep FAISS on-prem, can Redwood call into our index in our VPC?
[02:51] Diego Ramos: Yes - Private deployment or VPC peering with Dedicated can allow traffic to your index over secure links. For Hosted, you'd likely push vectors to an external managed vector DB like Pinecone or we can sync via secure upload.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: On dimensionality: we use 1536 dims now. Cost-wise, are there benefits to reducing to 1024 or 768? We worry about quality drop.
[03:15] Priya Shah: Right - we ran a quick eval and 1024 lost some recall on tail queries.
[03:20] Diego Ramos: Dimensionality tradeoffs are real: lower dims reduce storage and ANN search cost; quantization and PQ can shrink footprint. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and model/quant size based on your workload. Many customers do a small A/B: 1536 quantized to 8-bit PQ vs 1024 float - sometimes quantized 1536 keeps more signal than naive 1024 float. We can help with controlled evals.
[03:48] Maya Patel: Let's drill into throughput: assuming you want 200 QPS with a two-stage pipeline - dense ANN candidate retrieval then a lightweight reranker model - what are your latency budgets for each stage?
[03:59] Jordan Lee: Retrieval should be <40ms p95, reranker maybe <80ms p95. Index + network should be under 40.
[04:07] Diego Ramos: That checks out. For Dedicated, we can provision instances to hit those p95s; we do continuous batching to improve GPU efficiency while enforcing latency SLOs. For Hosted you'd see variable latency depending on load and your tier. For reranking on GPU, if your reranker is a small transformer we can run model quantized CPU or GPU. There are cost tradeoffs.
[04:29] Priya Shah: About hybrid search - we also want to combine BM25 signals with dense. Some of our tail queries need lexical signals. How does Redwood support that?
[04:38] Diego Ramos: We support hybrid scoring patterns: you can send sparse features (BM25 scores) alongside dense vectors and Redwood's reranker can consume both, or we can return candidate lists from two indices (sparse and dense) and merge client-side. We also have built-in rerankers that accept feature vectors plus embeddings.
[04:55] Evan Moore: Security: how are keys managed, and what about audit logs for search queries? We need to show auditors who accessed what.
[05:05] Diego Ramos: For Private and Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Hosted can use our KMS or allow customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans. Audit logs are a standard feature in Redwood Console - per-request metadata, token-level breakdowns, and retention settings. We also have SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, and admin audit trails.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: Great. For benchmarks, we want to run an apples-to-apples comparison: our current FAISS setup vs Redwood Dedicated hosting the index + reranker. What does that process look like?
[05:33] Diego Ramos: We'll provide a benchmark harness and sample runner that you can run in your infra. It measures recall@10, p95 latency, and cost per 1M queries. We can also run a Redwood-managed benchmark if you provide data + privacy consent. Diego: I'll send the harness and a sample dataset.
[05:50] Priya Shah: On costs: are embeddings generation and storage billed separately? How do batching and caching affect cost?
[05:58] Maya Patel: Hosted billing is per-embedding token/usage and per-query compute for reranks; Dedicated is a capacity model with committed monthly costs plus per-usage for burst. Caching (prefix/KV) and intelligent batching that Redwood Optimize recommends can drastically reduce per-query token counts and GPU time. We'll send a sample TCO showing point estimates for 200 QPS steady vs bursts.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas on compatibility? Some of our metadata pipelines rely on custom post-processing on vectors before insertion into FAISS.
[06:28] Diego Ramos: We can support pre-processing steps; our ingestion connectors are configurable. If you need exact byte-level compatibility with FAISS indexes, we can export vectors in FAISS-compatible formats. There can be minor differences with quantized formats; we'll surface that during benchmarking.
[06:45] Evan Moore: For Private deployment on-prem, how involved is the setup? We're on k8s with some EKS clusters.
[06:52] Diego Ramos: Private can run within your VPC or on-prem; we have a deployable control plane and runtime packages. For k8s/EKS we provide Helm charts and operators; typical install timeline is 2-4 weeks depending on networking and compliance checks. We also offer a hybrid where control plane is customer-managed and compute runs in our Dedicated pool.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: Timeline-wise, we want a pilot within Q2 and production by Q4 if benchmarks look good.
[07:16] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. To recap next steps: I'll send pricing and TCO, Diego will send the benchmark harness and sample runner, and Jordan will share vector schema and two query workloads. We'll schedule a follow-up pilot kickoff once the benchmark results look good.
[07:33] Priya Shah: Quick question - do you support zero-downtime index rebuilds or incremental indexing?
[07:38] Diego Ramos: Yes - we support incremental indexing strategies and background rebuilds with alias swapping; for large corpora we recommend sharded indexes with rolling rebuilds.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: Solid. Also, security docs - SOC2 + encryption + SSO - could you share those?
[07:54] Maya Patel: Absolutely, I'll include our security pack link in the email.
[07:58] Evan Moore: One more: can we limit data residency to eu-west-1 on Hosted?
[08:03] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have region pins for Hosted customers; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[08:11] Maya Patel: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll send the follow-ups within the timelines discussed and tentatively reconvene after your benchmark run.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.
[08:22] END
